claims.text: The feedstock is an equimolar W-Nb-Mo-Ta-V refractory high-entropy-alloy powder made from 99.5%-pure elemental powders.
The powder is prepared by ball milling, spray granulation with 2.5 wt.% starch at 40 wt.% solids, and 35 kW radiofrequency-plasma spheronization under Ar/H2.
The substrate is polished TC4 (Ti6Al4V) measuring 50 × 20 × 10 mm.
A 2 mm preset WNbMoTaV powder layer is laser clad onto TC4 at powers of 3.3–3.7 kW, with an optimum predicted near 3.5 kW.
Cladding uses a 5 mm spot, 600 mm/min scan speed, 20 mm defocus, and 99.99% He shielding at 15 L/min.
Wear testing uses a 4 mm Si3N4 ball, 20 N load, 2 mm reciprocating track, 1 Hz frequency, and 30 minute duration.
Near 3.5 kW, laser cladding will produce a dense coating metallurgically bonded to TC4.
The coating will be composed primarily of a fine, lattice-distorted BCC solid solution.
The coating will contain a minor Ti-rich phase caused by limited dilution from the TC4 substrate.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding will refine the coating grains.
Lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening in the BCC phase will increase coating hardness and abrasive-wear resistance.
Fine grains will provide grain-boundary strengthening that contributes to increased hardness and wear resistance.
A protective tribo-oxide layer may form during sliding and improve wear resistance.
Insufficient laser power may cause incomplete melting and coating defects.
Excessive laser power may cause over-burning and excessive substrate dilution, weakening the predicted benefits.
The optimized coating will have hardness significantly above the stated bare-TC4 baseline of 341.25 HV0.3.
The optimized coating will have wear-volume loss below the stated bare-TC4 baseline of 6.09×10^7 μm³ under identical testing conditions.
Performance will vary nonmonotonically with laser power, with 3.5 kW outperforming both 3.3 and 3.7 kW.
At powers outside the tested window, such as 3.1 or 3.9 kW, insufficient bonding, excessive dilution, or incomplete melting will prevent comparable improvement.
Failure at approximately 3.5 kW to increase hardness, reduce wear volume, or produce the predicted dense BCC structure with controlled Ti dilution would falsify the hypothesis.
